sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: The front matter of a 2011 WHO, UNFPA, UNAIDS and IPPF case study from Swaziland on linking sexual and reproductive health with HIV/AIDS services, in support of the Global Plan to eliminate new HIV infections among children. It contains the title pages, copyright and disclaimer notice with publisher contact details, acknowledgements of Swazi and international partner organizations and main contributors, and the table of contents.

sections.title: Prongs 1 and 2 – programming of elimination of mother-to-child transmission

summary.text: Defines the distinction between linkages and integration of sexual and reproductive health and HIV services, and notes a shift in global attention from preventing mother-to-child transmission alone towards recognizing links between maternal health, HIV and child survival under the Millennium Development Goals.

sections.extract: programming of elimination of mother-to-child transmission Key definitions In delineating the full scope of a linked SRH and HIV response, the following distinction has been made between linkages and integration:2 Linkages Bi-directional (two-way) synergies in policy, programmes, services and advocacy between SRH and HIV. This is a broad, human rights-based approach, of which service integration is a sub-set.

sections.title: The commitment towards elimination of new HIV infections among children by 2015 and keeping their mothers alive

summary.text: Explains the global commitment to eliminate new HIV infections among children by 2015 while keeping mothers alive, built on four prongs of comprehensive programming integrated with sexual and reproductive health. It highlights growing attention to the first two prongs, preventing HIV in women and preventing unintended pregnancies among women living with HIV. Tables set out the prongs and associated interventions such as family planning, blood safety, stigma reduction and prevention of gender-based violence.

sections.title: Background

summary.text: Describes the background to Swaziland's HIV epidemic, noting the world's highest adult HIV prevalence, very low life expectancy and a high proportion of pregnant women living with HIV. It closes with a statement by the Prime Minister to the UN General Assembly committing the country to reduce new infections among children to zero by 2015.

sections.extract: Swaziland is known for having the highest rate of adult HIV infection in the world, with a recent figure at 25.9%.14 Swaziland is also one of 22 low- and middle-income priority countries15 with the highest estimated numbers of pregnant women living with HIV. sections.title: Case study sites

summary.text: Profiles the case study sites in Swaziland, starting with the Family Life Association of Swaziland and its youth-friendly clinics offering integrated sexual and reproductive health and HIV services, alongside other service providers mapped across the country. It then documents promising practices addressing Prong 1, preventing HIV among women, and Prong 2, preventing unintended pregnancies among women living with HIV. The section covers community outreach, peer education, counselling, family planning and linked referral services. It ends with a checklist of questions that facilities can use to assess whether they provide these services and have built them into standard operating procedures.

sections.title: Key resources

summary.text: Lists key resources on linking sexual and reproductive health and HIV, including a linkages resource pack and the 2011–2015 strategic framework on preventing HIV and unintended pregnancies, each with a short description. Most are produced by UN agencies, IPPF and the Inter-Agency Task Team.

sections.extract: www.srhhivlinkages.org This resource pack aims to build a common understanding of SRH and HIV linkages and provide an overview of the current status of these linkages among key partners. It contains a wide variety of useful resources for organizations working in the SRH and HIV field and advocating on this issue.
